To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coralligenous and the maerl habitats are distributed in the Mediterranean Sea in a patchy manner, with a high degree of overlap, and that their distributions can be modelled with a reasonable accuracy using environmental predictors.

“Predictive models were developed to identify areas with the highest potential for coralligenous and/or maerl habitats in the Mediterranean Sea, and were compared against the current state of knowledge of their distribution”.

1) we have collated the most comprehensive spatial dataset of coralligenous outcrop and maerl bed distribution across the Mediterranean Sea, and 2) we have produced the first continuous predictive maps of coralligenous occurrence, as well as of maerl beds occurrence, across the basin, which are useful tools to support marine spatial planning and management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the understanding of the spatial distribution of these important bioconstructions across the Mediterranean Sea, with the aim to inform future marine conservation efforts.
the development of predictive models for two key habitats of the Mediterranean Sea, coralligenous outcrop and maerl bed habitats.
providing a comprehensive overview of the spatial distribution of coralline habitats across the Mediterranean, with a view to supporting effective conservation and management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coralligenous and/or maerl beds can be found in all Mediterranean coastal areas, but their distribution and abundance are very variable and depend on the local environmental conditions.
the coralligenous habitat occurs in the Mediterranean Sea from 0 to 200 m, and the maërl habitat from 0 to more than 300 m depth.

coralligenous outcrop distribution is mostly related to depth and bottom substrate, whereas maerl bed distribution is mostly related with the presence of sandy bottoms, and that the two habitats are mostly distributed in the western Mediterranean.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the collated occurrence data, and the derived distribution model outputs, can help addressing the challenges of developing basin-wide conservation plans and to guide future surveys and monitoring towards areas that are currently poorly sampled.

we have produced the first continuous maps for coralligenic and maërl beds across the whole Mediterranean Sea, and that these maps can help to guide the development of basin-wide spatial plans for the conservation of these two habitats.
